headline: Daily market snapshot — September 8, 2026
summary: US equity futures decline as Brent crude approaches $100/bbl amid escalating US-Iran conflict and Houthi strikes on Saudi energy sites. VIX holds near 14.53; gold at $4,432; 10Y yield 4.79%; Bitcoin ~$79,466.

headline: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq futures slip amid rising oil prices
summary: US stock futures fell at the start of a shortened post-holiday week as investors weighed surging oil prices, escalating Middle East hostilities, and the US-Canada trade war. Dow futures dropped 0.7%, S&P 500 futures fell 0.2%, and Nasdaq-100 contracts were just below flat.
key_facts: Oracle earnings due later in week

headline: Brent crude nears $100 after strikes on Saudi energy sites amid renewed Mideast hostilities
summary: Oil extended gains as attacks on Saudi energy facilities compounded fears of escalating US-Iran hostilities. The Saudi energy ministry said operations at certain facilities were halted after Houthi strikes wounded more than 70 people, sending Brent crude to $99.16 (+2.23%) and WTI to $94.46 (+3.26%).
key_facts: Saudi energy facilities struck by Houthi militants
Operations halted at certain Saudi energy sites

headline: US military strikes three Iranian oil tankers in retaliation for missile attacks
summary: The US military struck three Iranian oil tankers — including one near Kharg Island, Iran's main oil terminal — after Iran launched ballistic missiles toward two US Navy warships near the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM said two carriers were disabled and a third was destroyed, targeting vessels it claims financed IRGC proxy networks.
key_facts: US struck 3 Iranian oil tankers including one near Kharg Island
Iran fired ballistic missiles at 2 US Navy warships
Iran called strikes a war crime

headline: U.S. strikes Iran oil tankers for first time in retaliation for Hormuz strikes
summary: The US struck Iranian oil tankers for the first time as the Hormuz conflict intensified, establishing a new escalation threshold in the ongoing US-Iran standoff. The confrontation has disrupted global shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, tightening oil supply and pushing crude prices sharply higher.
key_facts: First US strike on Iranian oil tankers
Tit-for-tat attacks between US and Iran
Oil prices surge on supply concerns

headline: Goldman Sachs raises oil price forecasts by $5 for 2026 and 2027 on Hormuz disruption
summary: Goldman Sachs raised its Brent and WTI oil price forecasts by $5/bbl for Dec 2026 and 2027, citing ongoing Middle Eastern shipping disruptions it expects to continue into 2027. The bank now sees Brent at $85 for Dec 2026 and $80 in 2027; WTI at $80 and $75 respectively.
key_facts: Hormuz disruptions expected to persist into 2027

headline: Canada hits US with retaliatory tariffs on $27.6B of goods effective September 8
summary: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on over 700 American goods took effect on September 8, matching US tariffs dollar-for-dollar. Ottawa applied 15%, 25%, and 50% rates to approximately $27.6 billion of US imports, targeting sectors including steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, and electronics.
key_facts: Canada tariffs on $27.6B of US goods effective Sept 8
Steel and aluminum duties doubled to 50%
US had imposed 50% tariffs on Canadian steel/aluminum
PM Carney: Canada to match tariffs dollar-for-dollar

headline: Canada announces retaliatory tariffs on US goods as trade war escalates
summary: Canada announced it would impose retaliatory tariffs on $27.6 billion of US goods starting September 8, in response to the US imposing 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian products including hockey equipment, cement, liquor, and dairy. The escalating trade dispute threatens to raise consumer prices on both sides of the border.
key_facts: US tariffs: 50% on $20B of Canadian products effective Aug 22
Canada counter-tariffs: 15-50% on $27.6B of US imports from Sept 8
Focus sectors: steel, dairy, appliances, ag equipment, electronics
PM Carney says Canada 'at war' with US

headline: Asian markets broadly rise as Nikkei gains 2.12%, Kospi surges 4.61%
summary: Asian equities gained broadly ahead of Tuesday's US session, led by South Korea's Kospi (+4.61%) and Japan's Nikkei 225 (+2.12%). Mainland China's CSI 300 added 0.59%. Strong momentum was driven by tech heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics and strengthening yen bets on a BOJ rate hike.
key_facts: SK Hynix and Samsung led Korean advance

headline: European stocks close mixed as Stoxx 600 ends near flat; CAC 40 leads
summary: European stocks closed in mixed territory on Monday as the pan-European Stoxx 600 finished just below flat. France's CAC 40 led the main indexes, gaining 0.33%, followed by Italy's FTSE MIB (+0.25%). The UK's FTSE 100 fell 0.1% and Germany's DAX shed 0.25% amid Mideast uncertainty.

headline: BOJ eyeing September rate hike, faster pace of tightening, sources say
summary: The Bank of Japan is poised to raise interest rates as soon as its September 17-18 meeting and may accelerate its tightening pace beyond the current twice-a-year cadence, according to sources familiar with BOJ thinking. Governor Ueda's hawkish comments have sharply boosted rate hike bets and driven the yen higher.
key_facts: BOJ expected to hike at Sept 17-18 meeting
BOJ may accelerate above twice-a-year pace
Inflation concerns driven by Middle East conflict and AI demand
Yen surged more than 2% on hawkish BOJ comments

headline: Yen jumps to highest since February as BOJ rate hike bets mount
summary: The Japanese yen surged to its highest level since February, appreciating as much as 1% to 152.89 per dollar, as traders increasingly priced in a Bank of Japan rate hike in September. Analysts attributed the move to Governor Ueda's hawkish signals and rising Mideast-driven inflation concerns.
key_facts: BOJ rate hike bets cited as driver
Yen up 1% against dollar on the day

headline: August jobs report: US adds 162,000 jobs, blowing past 53,000 estimate; unemployment 4.1%
summary: The August nonfarm payrolls report dramatically beat expectations with 162,000 jobs added versus the 53,000 consensus estimate, while the unemployment rate held at 4.1%. Private payrolls added 127,000 versus an estimate of 45,000. June and July were revised up a combined 55,000.
key_facts: June revised up 11K; July revised up 44K

headline: Market prices 60.1% chance of Fed September rate hike after strong jobs report
summary: Following the blowout August jobs report (+162K vs +53K estimate), market-implied odds of a Fed rate hike at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting rose to 60.1% per CME FedWatch, down from 78.8% the previous morning. Three FOMC dissenters — Hammack, Kashkari, and Logan — have been vocal about the need to hike.
key_facts: 60.1% market-implied probability of September Fed hike
Dissenters: Hammack, Kashkari, Logan voted for hike
Chair Kevin Warsh held rates in July (9-3 vote)

headline: Gold slips, silver steadies as rate fears grip metals; gold at $4,431.75
summary: Gold edged lower on Tuesday as rising rate-hike expectations lifted real yields and pressured non-yielding assets. Spot gold traded at $4,431.75, consolidating after falling 0.62% on Monday to $4,404.98. The DXY held near 98.97, supported by the strong jobs data.
key_facts: Higher real yields weigh on non-yielding assets

headline: Bitcoin and Ethereum prices today, Monday September 7: Crypto investors on rate watch
summary: Bitcoin held near $79,466 and Ethereum near $2,514.80 on Monday as crypto investors closely monitored Federal Reserve rate hike expectations following the strong August jobs report. BTC futures were down 0.61% on Tuesday pre-market amid broader risk-off sentiment.
key_facts: Fed rate hike watch weighing on crypto
Bitcoin held above $81,000 the prior Friday

headline: IonQ hosts Investor Day at NYSE on September 8; SkyWater acquisition in spotlight
summary: IonQ held its 2026 Investor Day at the New York Stock Exchange at 12:30 PM ET on September 8, headlined by Chairman/CEO Niccolo De Masi and featuring the newly integrated SkyWater semiconductor fabrication acquisition. Jefferies identified the event as the next major catalyst for IONQ stock, noting 44 of 52 analysts rate it a buy with a median price target of $65.
key_facts: IonQ Investor Day at NYSE, Sept 8 at 12:30 PM ET

headline: IonQ Q2 revenue surges 287% YoY to ~$80M; FY2026 guidance raised to $280-290M
summary: IonQ reported second-quarter revenue growth of 287% year-over-year to approximately $80 million, driven by quantum computing contract wins and the SkyWater Technology acquisition completed in late July. Management raised its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance from $225-245 million to $280-290 million, with analysts watching for multiyear revenue targets at the September 8 Investor Day.
key_facts: SkyWater gives IonQ its own semiconductor fab

headline: SanDisk rises pre-market as tech giants lock in memory supply through 2031 amid NAND shortage
summary: SanDisk (SNDK) was among top pre-market gainers on Tuesday as news broke that major technology companies had secured long-term NAND memory supply agreements through 2031, highlighting an extended global shortage. SanDisk's entire 2026 enterprise AI storage capacity is sold out under long-term contracts, underpinning a $42 billion backlog.
key_facts: Tech giants secured long-term NAND supply through 2031
NAND shortage expected to persist to end of decade
Entire 2026 enterprise AI storage capacity sold out
One-third of FY2027 production under long-term agreements

headline: SanDisk stock rockets 857% in first half of 2026 on AI memory boom
summary: SanDisk (SNDK) surged 857.8% in the first half of 2026, making it one of the top-performing stocks on any major US exchange, driven by explosive demand for NAND flash memory from AI data centers and a persistent global supply shortage. The company's sold-out capacity and growing backlog have attracted significant institutional interest.
key_facts: Driven by AI data center NAND demand
Structural NAND shortage expected through end of decade
5 long-term supply agreements covering 1/3 of FY2027 production

headline: Broadcom Q3 FY2026: Revenue $29.59B, AI semiconductor revenue tripled to $16.7B YoY
summary: Broadcom reported record fiscal Q3 revenue of $29.59 billion (up 86% YoY) and diluted EPS of $2.68 (up 215% YoY), driven by explosive AI chip demand from six XPU customers including Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI. AI semiconductor revenue surged 221% to $16.7 billion. The company raised its FY2026 AI revenue guidance to $58 billion.
key_facts: FY2026 AI revenue guidance raised to $58B
6 XPU customers: Google, Anthropic, OpenAI and others

headline: Broadcom forecasts $58B in FY2026 AI revenue; outlines $115B in 2027, $230B in 2028
summary: Broadcom provided a sweeping multi-year AI revenue roadmap, guiding for $58 billion in FY2026 (+186% YoY), $115 billion in FY2027, and $230 billion in FY2028, reflecting the company's dominant position as a custom AI accelerator (ASIC) supplier with 70-80% market share in that segment.

headline: Oracle (ORCL) set to report Q1 FY2027 earnings September 10; cloud growth in focus
summary: Oracle is expected to report fiscal Q1 2027 results on September 10, with analyst consensus calling for revenue of $19.13 billion and non-GAAP EPS of approximately $1.73, in line with guidance of $1.72-$1.76. Cloud infrastructure and AI-related contracts remain the key market focus.
key_facts: AI infrastructure contracts and cloud growth in focus

headline: Flex acquires EPC Power for $4.4B to expand AI data center power conversion portfolio
summary: Flex announced an agreement to acquire EPC Power, a designer of power conversion equipment for AI data centers and grid applications, for $4.4 billion. The deal adds 800V data center power architectures and solid-state transformers to Flex's Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment, which the company plans to spin off as an independent public company in Q1 2027.
key_facts: Flex to acquire EPC Power for $4.4B
EPC specializes in 800V AI data center power architectures
Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment to IPO Q1 2027
Goldman Sachs sold EPC Power from its alternatives portfolio

headline: Aon acquires USI Insurance from KKR in $17B deal to build middle-market platform
summary: Aon agreed to acquire USI Insurance Services from KKR and other shareholders for $17 billion in cash, targeting the US middle market in a strategic extension of its 2024 NFP acquisition. USI generates ~$3 billion in annual revenue with 10,500+ employees across 200 offices. Aon expects $395 million in run-rate synergies and will fund the deal entirely through new debt.
key_facts: Aon acquires USI for $17B in cash
Expected synergies: $395M run-rate net adjusted EBITDA
Aon to fund with new debt, remain investment-grade

headline: Chevron to invest $7B in Venezuela to double oil output to 600,000 bbl/day
summary: Chevron announced $7 billion in planned investments over five years to more than double its Venezuelan output to approximately 600,000 barrels per day, following updated JV terms and new Orinoco Belt acreage. The deal follows a Trump administration-brokered agreement with Venezuela announced August 28 involving a private joint venture over fields with 65 billion barrels of petroleum.
key_facts: Chevron to invest $7B over 5 years in Venezuela
New acreage in Carabobo-1 and Carabobo-2-South-A of Orinoco Belt
Trump-Venezuela deal announced Aug 28 (65B bbl fields)

headline: TSMC raises FY2026 revenue growth guidance to above 40% on AI chip demand; Q3 guided $44.6-45.8B
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to slightly above 40%, up from more than 30%, after Q2 profit hit a record. TSMC guided Q3 revenue of $44.6-45.8 billion and raised 2026 capital expenditure to $60-64 billion. The company committed an additional $100 billion to Arizona manufacturing.
key_facts: FY2026 revenue guidance raised to >40% growth (from >30%)

headline: BNP Paribas raises Samsara price target from $40 to $55, maintains Outperform
summary: BNP Paribas analyst Andrew DeGasperi raised the price target on Samsara from $40 to $55 while maintaining an Outperform rating, reflecting improved confidence in the fleet telematics company's growth trajectory.

headline: Macquarie raises Zscaler price target from $172 to $200, maintains Outperform
summary: Macquarie analyst Steve Koenig raised the Zscaler price target from $172 to $200 while maintaining an Outperform rating, following Zscaler's strong Q4 FY2026 earnings beat in which EPS came in at $1.19 versus a $1.09 consensus.

headline: Macquarie raises Snowflake price target from $200 to $350, maintains Neutral
summary: Macquarie analyst Steve Koenig raised the Snowflake price target from $200 to $350 while maintaining a Neutral rating, citing improved growth visibility following Snowflake's Q2 FY2027 results in which revenue rose 35% year-over-year and came in 22% above estimates.
key_facts: SNOW Q2 FY2027 revenue +35% YoY, +22% vs estimates

headline: Scotiabank raises MongoDB price target from $395 to $440, maintains Sector Outperform
summary: Scotiabank analyst Patrick Colville raised the MongoDB price target from $395 to $440 while maintaining a Sector Outperform rating, reflecting improved confidence in the database company's growth and AI-driven workload adoption.
key_facts: Scotiabank Sector Outperform maintained on MDB

headline: UBS lowers ConocoPhillips price target from $155 to $143, maintains Buy
summary: UBS analyst Josh Silverstein lowered the ConocoPhillips price target from $155 to $143 while maintaining a Buy rating. The trim likely reflects updated commodity price assumptions and capital allocation estimates despite still constructive long-term oil market view.

headline: Morgan Stanley lowers VICI Properties price target from $38 to $31, maintains Equal-Weight
summary: Morgan Stanley analyst Ronald Kamdem lowered the VICI Properties price target from $38 to $31 while maintaining an Equal-Weight rating. The reduction likely reflects higher-for-longer rate expectations weighing on REIT valuations as the Fed eyes a September hike.
key_facts: Morgan Stanley Equal-Weight maintained on VICI
Higher rate expectations weighing on REITs

headline: UBS lowers Constellium price target from $38 to $35, maintains Buy
summary: UBS analyst Alex Stansbury lowered the Constellium price target from $38 to $35 while maintaining a Buy rating on the aluminum products company, reflecting more cautious near-term demand assumptions amid macro uncertainty.

headline: US stocks closed mostly lower Friday after blowout jobs report; S&P -0.4%, Dow -272 points, Nasdaq +0.2%
summary: US stocks closed mostly lower on Friday, September 5, after the blowout August jobs report gave the Fed more room to raise interest rates. The S&P 500 lost 0.4%, the Dow shed 272 points, while the Nasdaq modestly outperformed with a 0.2% gain. The 10-year Treasury yield jumped nearly 3 basis points to 4.79%.
key_facts: Strong jobs report drove rate hike expectations

headline: Energy sector leads all S&P sectors with 43% YTD gain in 2026 on oil price surge
summary: The energy sector is the top-performing S&P 500 sector in 2026, up approximately 43% year-to-date, driven by surging crude oil prices amid Middle East conflict and supply disruptions. The SPDR S&P Oil & Gas E&P ETF (XOP) hit a multi-year high, and refiners including Valero (+52.7%), Marathon (+50.9%), and Phillips 66 (+42.3%) all outperformed.

headline: Pre-market movers Sept 8: IonQ leads gains on Investor Day; SanDisk higher on NAND demand
summary: Among notable pre-market movers on Tuesday, IonQ (IONQ) traded significantly higher ahead of its 12:30 PM ET Investor Day at the NYSE, supported by reports of institutional purchases by UBS and Man Group. SanDisk (SNDK) also moved higher on news that major tech companies secured long-term NAND supply through 2031.
key_facts: IONQ among top pre-market gainers Sept 8
Institutional buyers: UBS, Man Group in IONQ
SNDK higher on long-term NAND supply deals

headline: Refiners are quiet winners in 2026: Valero, Marathon, Phillips 66 hit 52-week highs
summary: US oil refiners Valero Energy, Marathon Petroleum, and Phillips 66 have each hit 52-week highs in 2026, benefiting from wide crack spreads amid elevated crude oil prices and strong fuel demand. Valero is the top performer with a 52.7% gain, followed by Marathon at 50.9% and Phillips 66 at 42.3%.
key_facts: Wide crack spreads on elevated crude prices

headline: Oil stocks surge as Middle East conflict pushes energy prices higher; XLE up 43% YTD
summary: Oil and gas exploration and production stocks surged as escalating Middle East conflict pushed energy prices higher, with Brent crude nearing $100/bbl. The energy sector ETF XLE is up 43% YTD, and individual names including ExxonMobil, Chevron, ConocoPhillips, and Marathon Petroleum are outperforming the broader market.
key_facts: Middle East conflict driving energy outperformance
ExxonMobil, Chevron, COP among top performers

headline: Brent crude tops $100 for first time since 2022 as Middle East tensions shake markets
summary: Brent crude oil crossed the $100 per barrel threshold for the first time since 2022 on September 8, as escalating US-Iran military strikes, Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure, and continued Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions combined to tighten global oil supply sharply.
key_facts: Brent crosses $100/bbl for first time since 2022
Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites
Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions ongoing
Goldman Sachs raised Brent Dec 2026 forecast to $85/bbl

headline: Divided Fed voted 9-3 to hold rates at 3.5-3.75% in July; September hike odds climb
summary: The FOMC voted 9-3 to leave the federal funds rate unchanged at 3.5%-3.75% at its July meeting, with dissenters Beth Hammack, Neel Kashkari, and Lorie Logan pushing for a hike. Following the strong August jobs report, market odds for a September hike climbed to 60.1%, with the September 15-16 meeting now viewed as a critical decision point.
key_facts: Fed held rates at 3.5-3.75% in July, vote 9-3
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh held rate post-strong jobs data
September 15-16 FOMC meeting is next decision

headline: BOJ's Ueda hints at September rate hike as bets on move mount
summary: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda signaled that a rate hike is likely when the board convenes for its September 17-18 meeting, citing upside price risks from Middle East conflict, strong AI demand, and yen weakness. Ueda said officials will decide policy with upside inflation risks in mind.
key_facts: BOJ Governor Ueda hints September rate hike likely
Inflation upside risks: Middle East oil, AI demand, weak yen
Rate hike would be above twice-a-year pace

headline: Daily Market Outlook September 8: Oil near $100, Canada tariffs live, BOJ on watch
summary: Tuesday's market session is dominated by three key themes: Brent crude nearing $100/bbl on Houthi strikes and the US-Iran tanker war; Canada's new retaliatory tariffs on $27.6 billion of US goods taking effect today; and rising bets on a Bank of Japan September rate hike. US equities face headwinds from all three.

headline: Asia fundamental forecast Sept 8: BOJ tightening bets, strong Kospi tech rally, yen strength
summary: Asia-Pacific markets heading into Tuesday's session show significant divergence, with Japan's stronger-than-expected GDP and wage growth reinforcing BOJ tightening expectations. Overnight the Nikkei added 2.12%, Kospi surged 4.61% led by SK Hynix and Samsung, while the yen appreciated to 152.89, pressuring export-sensitive names.

headline: Europe fundamental forecast Sept 8: Stoxx 600 near flat, oil concerns linger
summary: European markets headed into Tuesday's US session in mixed territory after Monday's near-flat close in the Stoxx 600. Renewed Iran-US tensions are keeping Brent crude near $97-98, and the ECB's interest rate outlook remains uncertain. The strong US jobs report complicates any dovish pivot from global central banks.
key_facts: Brent crude $97-98 keeping energy costs elevated
Strong US jobs data complicates global dovish pivot

headline: US added 162,000 jobs in August, but wage growth continues to lag inflation
summary: The US economy added 162,000 jobs in August, far beating the 53,000 consensus, but wage growth continued to trail inflation, limiting the boost to real purchasing power. The Fed is expected to look closely at the September 11 CPI release before finalizing its September 15-16 rate decision.

headline: August jobs report: US adds 162,000 positions, unemployment at 4.1%
summary: The August nonfarm payrolls report was a significant beat, with 162,000 jobs added versus the 53,000 forecast. Private payrolls rose 127,000 against an estimated 45,000. The data drove a spike in rate hike expectations and pushed the 10-year Treasury yield up 3 basis points to 4.79%.
key_facts: Fed Sep hike probability rose to ~60%
